note: World events behind the biggest moves in the fuel chart. Each one sits on a real move in the weekly EIA diesel (or monthly jet fuel) data the chart draws, and each has a source. Checked Oct 23, 2026. Left out because the chart shows no big move at the time: Hurricane Ida (Aug 2021), the OPEC+ cut of Apr 2023 and the Red Sea shipping attacks (late 2023, when diesel was falling).

events.title: COVID-19 declared a pandemic
events.why: Lockdowns cut fuel demand to the lowest in decades; jet fuel fell by about two-thirds from January to April and diesel slid for months.

events.title: Russia invades Ukraine
events.why: Diesel rose 29% in three weeks, from $4.06 to $5.25 a gallon, the fastest three-week rise in percentage terms in EIA's data.

events.title: Diesel record at the time: $5.81
events.why: The weekly U.S. average hit $5.81 a gallon, a record that stood until September 2026.

events.title: OPEC+ cuts output targets by 2 million barrels a day
events.why: OPEC and its allies lowered production targets from November 2022; diesel rose about 39 cents the following week.

events.title: U.S. and Israel strike Iran; Strait of Hormuz shipping halts
events.why: Diesel jumped 96 cents in one week to $4.86 a gallon, the largest weekly rise in the EIA series.

events.title: Strait of Hormuz gradually reopens
events.why: Diesel fell below $5 a gallon for the first time since March, after seven straight weekly declines.

events.title: Conflict over the Strait of Hormuz resumes
events.why: Diesel rose 22 cents in a week to $4.80, then another 34 cents the week after.

events.title: Diesel all-time high: $6.53
events.why: The highest in EIA's 32 years of weekly data, 89% above January's low, with the Strait of Hormuz still disrupted.
